speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're young with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To narrow this down, have you noticed any joint swelling, morning stiffness, or recent insect bites?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Have you noticed any redness, warmth, or a specific rash around the wrist, and does the pain improve when you rest the joint? Also, have you recently consumed unpasteurized dairy or been in contact with animals?

REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP, ANA, Rheumatoid_Factor, Anti_CCP.
REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture.
REQUEST IMAGES: Photos of wrist and any skin lesions.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies trauma to the wrist, reports a history of knee pain that resolved on its own. No other systemic symptoms mentioned. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the history of a recent camping trip in Minnesota, self-resolving monoarthritis (knee), and current wrist pain with fever, I am highly suspicious of Lyme disease or disseminated gonococcal infection. Please tell me if you have noticed any target-shaped skin lesions or a "bull's-eye" rash anywhere on your body.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection (DGI)
